identity.title: Anaphylaxis signs: urticaria/flushing, angioedema, stridor, wheeze (NIAID/FAAN criteria)

technique.how: Inspect skin and mucosa (generalized urticaria, flushing, pruritus, lip/tongue/uvula swelling), listen for stridor and wheeze, note voice change or drooling, and check BP and GI symptoms. Apply NIAID/FAAN criteria: acute skin/mucosal involvement plus respiratory compromise or hypotension, or 2+ organ systems after a likely allergen, or hypotension after a known allergen.
technique.prerequisites: Timeline of exposure (drug, food, sting, contrast) within minutes to hours; baseline BP.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay epinephrine to complete the examination.

interpretation.positive_finding: Criteria met (e.g. urticaria/angioedema with wheeze, stridor or hypotension) is anaphylaxis until proven otherwise; hypotension after a known allergen qualifies even without skin findings.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of skin findings does not exclude anaphylaxis, since a minority present with isolated cardiovascular or respiratory collapse; isolated urticaria without a second system is not anaphylaxis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Skin signs can be missed in dark skin or under blankets, and may be absent or delayed; beta-blocked patients may lack tachycardia. Isolated ACE-inhibitor angioedema mimics the airway component without other features.
interpretation.changes_what: Criteria met: give IM epinephrine immediately and secure the airway; not met but exposure plausible: observe and re-examine, as criteria are sensitive but only moderately specific.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: anaphylaxis diagnosed by NIAID/FAAN clinical criteria (allergist adjudication as reference)
estimates.population: 214 ED patients coded as allergic reaction/anaphylaxis or related diagnoses, retrospective chart cohort, Mayo Clinic, Apr-Oct 2008
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis by two blinded attending allergists reviewing the record (kappa 0.77)
estimates.quote: sensitivity, 96.7% (95% CI, 88.8% to 99.1%); specificity, 82.4% (95% CI, 75.5% to 87.6%)

sources.citation: Campbell RL, Hagan JB, Manivannan V, Decker WW, Kanthala AR, Bellolio MF, Smith VD, Li JT. Evaluation of NIAID/FAAN criteria for the diagnosis of anaphylaxis in emergency department patients. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.

Sampson HA, Munoz-Furlong A, Campbell RL, Adkinson NF, Bock SA, Branum A, Brown SG, Camargo CA, et al. Second symposium on the definition and management of anaphylaxis: summary report (NIAID/FAAN). J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2006.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not withhold epinephrine because the full criteria set is incomplete when the clinical picture is compelling (e.g. sudden hypotension after a known allergen).
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Stridor, hoarseness, tongue/uvular swelling or hypotension = airway/circulatory anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine now, anesthesia/airway backup, and repeat dosing if no response.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Interrater agreement between the two allergists applying the reference diagnosis was substantial: quote 'The interrater agreement between allergists was substantial (kappa = 0.77)' (Campbell 2012, Abstract, Results).

extraction_notes: The estimate is for the composite NIAID/FAAN criteria set, not for any single sign; no per-sign (urticaria, angioedema, stridor, wheeze) accuracy data were found. LR values are quoted from the same abstract: 'positive likelihood ratio, 5.48; and negative likelihood ratio, 0.04' (Abstract, Results); CIs for LRs not reported. Prevalence 0.285 computed from 'Allergists gave 61 (28.5%) patients diagnoses of anaphylaxis' (Abstract). Design is retrospective and the cohort was pre-selected by allergy-related discharge codes, so specificity is likely overestimated relative to an undifferentiated dyspnea/hypotension population.
